Lambeth's population increased by around 14,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 320,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Lambeth increased by 4.8%, from around 303,100 in 2011 to around 317,700 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of London (7.7%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Lambeth was home to around 84.5 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 80.7 in 2011. This area was among the top 2% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Lambeth than across London

Median age increased

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Lambeth increased by two years, from 31 to 33 years of age.

This area had a lower average (median) age than London as a whole in 2021 (35 years) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 15,800 (an increase of 44.0%), while the number of residents aged 4 years and under fell by just over 5,400 (26.3% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 4.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Lambeth residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 186,600 Lambeth residents said they were born in England. This represented 58.7% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 176,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 58.1% of Lambeth's population.

South American countries were the next most represented, with around 13,200 Lambeth residents reporting one of these countries as their country of birth (4.1%). This figure was up from around 9,000 in 2011, which at the time represented 3.0% of the population of Lambeth.

The number of Lambeth residents born in Jamaica fell from just over 9,700 in 2011 (3.2% of the local population) to just over 7,800 in 2021 (2.5%).

In 2021, 58.7% of Lambeth residents reported their country of birth as England

Family in Lambeth

The percentage of lone-parent households fell in Lambeth, but rose across London.

In Lambeth, the percentage of households including a lone parent fell from 14.7% in 2011 to 14.3% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 12.7% to 13.3%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Lambeth fell from 12.3% to 11.9%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 2.7% to 3.3%.

The percentage of households including a lone parent in Lambeth decreased by 0.4 percentage points

National identity in Lambeth

Lambeth saw England's joint third-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Waltham Forest) in the proportion of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK (from 25.6% in 2011 to 22.8% in 2021).

England's largest decreases in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK occurred in Kensington and Chelsea (from 37.7% to 32.0%) followed by Westminster (from 36.6% to 32.4%).

Despite the decrease, Lambeth was in the highest 10% of English local authority areas for the share of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in 2021.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Lambeth decreased by 2.8 percentage points

Employment in Lambeth

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed increased here, but fell across England.

In Lambeth, the percentage who were employed rose from 64.6% in 2011 to 66.1% in 2021, while across England it fell from 56.5% to 55.7%. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 58.6% to 59.4%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Lambeth fell from 5.8% to 4.6%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) decreased from 8.9% to 8.3%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Lambeth increased by 1.5 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

In 2021, 9.1% of Lambeth residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 6.8% in 2011.

This area had Greater London's third lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week. Across the region, only City of London (7.2%) and Wandsworth (8.1%) had a lower percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week.

Because of its small size, comparisons to City of London should be made with caution.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Lambeth increased by 2.3 percentage points

Unpaid care in Lambeth

In 2021, 3.6% of Lambeth residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 5.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.3% in 2011. The proportion of Lambeth residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 2.1% to 1.9%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater across London (2.6 percentage points, from 6.4% to 3.8%) than in Lambeth (1.8 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Lambeth decreased by 1.8 percentage points

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in nearby Southwark (5.0 percentage points) than in Lambeth (2.1 percentage points).

In Lambeth, the percentage of private renting increased from 29.3% in 2011 to 31.4% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Southwark increased from 23.7% to 28.7%.

The rate of social renting in Lambeth fell from 35.1% to 33.6%, while the rate of home ownership remained at 33.0%.

Private renting in Lambeth increased by 2.1 percentage points

Health in Lambeth

In 2021, 49.9% of Lambeth residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 44.0% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 32.6% to 31.2%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Lambeth residents describing their health as "very bad" decreased from 2.0% to 1.5%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.8% to 4.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Lambeth increased by 5.9 percentage points

Disability in Lambeth

In 2021, 7.8% of Lambeth residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 10.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater in Lambeth (2.9 percentage points) than across London (2.3 percentage points, from 9.4% to 7.1%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Lambeth decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Lambeth

In 2021, 5.7% of Lambeth residents identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group"), up from 2.4% in 2011. The 3.2 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across London, the percentage of people from the "Other ethnic groups" ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 3.4% to 6.3%, while across England the percentage increased from 1.0% to 2.2%.

In 2021, 55.0% of people in Lambeth identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 57.1% in 2011), while 24.0% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 25.9% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 7.6% in 2011 to 8.1% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 5.7% of usual residents in Lambeth identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group")

Religion in Lambeth

In 2021, 37.5% of Lambeth residents reported having "No religion", up from 28.0% in 2011. The rise of 9.5 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Lambeth. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across London, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 21.0% to 27.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 43.7% of people in Lambeth described themselves as Christian (down from 53.1%), while 8.1% described themselves as Muslim (up from 7.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 37.5% of usual residents in Lambeth reported having "No religion"

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Lambeth residents aged 16 years and over, 62.2% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 58.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in four people (25.6%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 27.0% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Lambeth that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 7.3% to 7.0%.

This area had the country's highest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership and the lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership). Islington had England's next-highest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (62.0%), while Hambleton and New Forest had the country's joint lowest percentage (26.9%).

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Lambeth increased by 3.8 percentage points
